observations.body: After stored guilt and delayed birth imagery, the speech asks whether Ephraim will be ransomed from Sheol and redeemed from death, then addresses death and Sheol directly.
observations.label: Ransom from Sheol becomes a taunt against death

observations.body: The passage presents Ransoming and redeeming as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Ransoming and redeeming

observations.body: The passage places Ephraim beside Ransoming and redeeming.
observations.label: Ephraim

payload.posture: Read Hosea 13:12–14 as one movement in the resurrection, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.title: Ransom from Sheol becomes a taunt against death
